title: The Protocol of the Deep
premise: Jonah Winterbourne investigates impossible insurance claims across the fractured colonies of the Meridian Belt, where two human factions have been at cold war since the Silence severed their communication networks. When the freighter Cassiopeia's Wake returns from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward, Jonah is sent to assess a claim that shouldn't exist — and discovers the ship carries a decoded protocol that could reopen contact between the warring worlds. Hunted by both governments, betrayed by his own handler, and bound to the ship's youngest-again captain who remembers a future no one else lived, Jonah must carry the message through the last jump window of the season. He delivers it at terrible cost: the truth ends the war but exposes him as the son of the admiral who caused the Silence, and he chooses exile aboard the Wake rather than let either side make him a symbol.
about_author: Rafael Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to losses among the stars. They write from a coastal town whose lighthouse they claim is 'the only honest machine I've ever met.'

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Winterbourne works a routine claim on a station that shouldn't have survived a reactor breach, establishing his method: accidents are never impossible, only unprofitable to explain. A coded summons from his handler, Vess, interrupts him. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; the reader feels a man who trusts paperwork more than people.

chapters.title: A Ship That Forgot Its Age
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At Meridian Station, Jonah inspects the returned Cassiopeia's Wake: hull records say forty years out, crew manifests list children who scan as those same sailors de-aged. Captain Ilsa Reyes-Mbeki, now twenty-two in body, recognizes Jonah by name though they've never met. Emotional beat: uncanny dread sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: The Claim That Cannot Pay
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The insurer wants the ship declared a total loss and sealed; the crew refuses to disembark. Jonah finds the cargo manifest lists one item with no value column: a sealed data core labeled PROTOCOL. Vess orders him to certify and walk away. Emotional beat: first crack in his faith in systems.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Years Old Twice
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Flashback-threaded chapter: Ilsa recalls the deep-space anomaly that reversed them, and the older version of herself who left a message for her younger self — including a warning about a man named Winterbourne. Emotional beat: grief for a self she outlived; tenderness toward strangers she already knows.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Dock
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Naval officers from both warring factions arrive simultaneously to seize the Wake. Jonah plays the neutral investigator, stalling both sides while smuggling Ilsa's core into his claim case. Emotional beat: the thrill of deception curdling into fear as he realizes he's now evidence.

chapters.title: What the Silence Buried
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She tells Jonah the truth the core holds: the Silence wasn't an accident of physics but a weapon test by Admiral Edric Winterbourne — Jonah's father — that severed interstellar communication to prevent a first strike. Emotional beat: betrayal arriving like cold water; Jonah's identity becomes the story's fault line.

chapters.title: Handler's Gambit
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Vess reveals the insurer is a front for the Eastern Combine; the claim was bait to locate the core. She offers Jonah immunity and a new life if he surrenders it. He refuses, and realizes she anticipated that too. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal — every ally is a ledger entry.

chapters.title: The Crew Who Remember Tomorrow
chapters.summary: POV ensemble via Ilsa. The de-aged crew votes on whether to trust Jonah; engineer Sef Okafor argues against, citing what the future-Jonah did in their timeline. Ilsa overrules him. Emotional beat: democracy under pressure; hope choosing to be naive on purpose.

chapters.title: Dockside Fire
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. An 'impossible' fire destroys the Wake's berth logs — Jonah's own investigative instincts tell him it's Vess erasing the paper trail. Two crew members are caught outside the shield. One survives. Emotional beat: guilt as tuition; the price of survival begins accruing interest.

chapters.title: Admiral's Son
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah breaks into the naval archive and finds his father's sealed testimony about the Silence — and learns Edric Winterbourne is still alive, in cryo, held as a bargaining chip by the Western Directorate. Emotional beat: the investigation turns inward; he was always the accident being investigated.

chapters.title: Jump Window Mathematics
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Navigator calculations show one corridor opens in nine days and won't recur for a year; delivering the Protocol requires crossing both blockades. Ilsa and Jonah plan the run, arguing about whether truth delivered by force is still truth. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in logistics; love deferred for duty.

chapters.title: Vess Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Vess boards under truce flag with an offer from the Combine: broadcast the Protocol themselves, edited, blaming the West. She shows Jonah proof his father ordered the Silence knowingly. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable; the corrupt offer wears honesty's clothes.

chapters.title: The Edited Truth
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa decrypts the full core and finds the future-crew recorded everything, including atrocities committed by both sides after the Silence. There is no clean version to deliver. Emotional beat: disillusionment as maturation; truth is heavy because it is whole.

chapters.title: Sef's Mutiny
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Believing delivery will trigger the war the future-crew barely survived, Sef seizes engineering and begins purging the core. Jonah talks him down not with argument but by volunteering to stand trial alongside the message. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — obedience to people, not plans.

chapters.title: Cryo Bay Seven
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The Wake diverts to retrieve Edric Winterbourne as living testimony. Father and son meet across thirty frozen years; Edric defends the Silence as the only alternative to genocide. Emotional beat: the book's moral center — power corrupted by the sincere belief it was saving everyone.

chapters.title: Blockade Run
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The jump run: the Wake threads between Eastern picket lines while Vess, true to form, feeds their course to both navies to force a confrontation she can film. Casualties mount. Emotional beat: kinetic terror; survival purchased openly, itemized in lives.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Damaged short of the corridor, the Wake can't make the window — unless someone stays behind to hold the relay open manually. Sef takes the post without asking permission. The ship jumps as his signal gutters out. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony; the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. On the far side, the Wake transmits the complete Protocol and archive to both homeworlds simultaneously — no edits, no exclusives. Fleets hold fire as the record unfolds. Emotional beat: held breath; truth landing not as triumph but as verdict.

chapters.title: The War That Didn't Start
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Armistice talks convene aboard the Wake; both sides want Jonah silenced or sanctified. He testifies to his father's crimes and his own complicity in hiding the core, then declines every offered role. Emotional beat: refusal as integrity; ending the war by refusing to profit from it.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The colonies ratify the Meridian Accord, reopening channels. Ilsa, aging forward again into a life she never chose, is offered her old command and instead asks for a survey route — somewhere quiet. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; survivors learning to want small things.

chapters.title: Exile's Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah signs on as the Wake's permanent claims investigator — the man who prices impossibilities, sailing routes no government owns. Vess sends one last message: an opening back home, declined unread. Emotional beat: peace chosen over belonging; the long route as home.

chapters.title: The Honest Machine
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, coda. Months later, the Wake answers a distress call from a ship returning early — aged backward again, carrying a second core. Jonah smiles, opens a fresh claim file, and signals Ilsa: 'We're going to need a bigger ledger.' Emotional beat: wonder restored; the story ends where investigation begins.
